newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-up $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-up $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen steady to up $0.50 per cwt higher on support from light hog marketings, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog marketings Monday were estimated at 90,000 head, compared with 102,000 a week ago and 99,000 a year ago, USDA statisitcs showed.
Demand for the hogs was seen strong as several plants that were closed on Monday for a "floating holiday" reopen on Tuesday, the dealers said.
Potential gains could be offset, however, if pork product prices trend weaker, the dealers said.
Fresh pork prices at midday were quoted $2.00 per cwt lower for pork bellies and lean trimmings and steady for hams in the central U.S. carlot pork report by USDA.
There were 10 loads of pork and three loads of trimmed and processed pork sold by midday, the statistics showed.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant were seen at $61.00, dealers said.
Illinois top hog prices at the plant could range $61.00 to $61.50. Indiana/Ohio top hog prices were expected at $61.00
